The utility monopoly would generate about $70 in rent per landing on average. That is not as strong as building houses on an orange set.

A complete orange set with houses would be devastating. Three houses on each property cost $300, leaving p4 with $300 to spend. That is enough for a full house build, and the rent would be extremely high.

This trade violates my prior strategy of never giving away properties that complete an opponent's set. The orange monopoly is the highest ROI color group, so handing over Tennessee is especially costly. I would not gain a buildable monopoly from this deal, since utilities cannot be improved with houses.

The $473 value proposition is irrelevant because deed value does not reflect monopoly worth. I am now considering a counter-offer. I would only trade Tennessee if the new deal also gives me a strong buildable set without handing p4 the orange monopoly. I cannot easily complete a color set through other trades, since p2 would not give up both Indiana and Illinois for Tennessee.

Oriental Avenue would not help me because I lack the other light blue properties. Denying p3 that set is not worth giving up Tennessee.

The correct decision is to reject the offer. This is a trap. p4 bought New York specifically to pair with St. James, and they immediately offered this trade because they know it completes an orange monopoly. That is exactly what I must avoid.

Two houses on each orange property would cost $600 and yield over $600 in rent per landing. That is devastating. Even one landing could bankrupt me. I will reject the offer. I am now considering counter-offers that do not give p4 the orange monopoly.

I rejected offering Water Works because that would complete p4's utility set. I also decided not to trade Short Line or Marvin Gardens, since Marvin is a valuable yellow blocker. I am still searching for a counter-offer that gives me a strong buildable set without handing p4 the orange monopoly.

I will not counter this offer. Any counter could signal that I am willing to trade Tennessee, which would invite further negotiation and eventually leak the property. I will simply reject it.

I will reject the offer publicly and keep Tennessee. Completing an opponent's orange set is not for sale.

With $687 remaining, I am considering denial buys for Virginia Avenue, B&O Railroad, North Carolina Avenue, and Mediterranean Avenue. Virginia is the most urgent because p3 needs it to complete a pink monopoly.

p4 still holds two of the three orange properties and will continue pressuring for Tennessee. I must never sell it.

p2 still wants Kentucky Avenue.
